analysis:
PORTFOLIO REVIEW: All four existing positions remain within normal variance and no thesis-break conditions are present. AMP (+3.11%) is the strongest; MCO (+1.03%) is fine; BR (-0.50%) and NVDA (-2.97%) are within stop buffers and fundamentals remain intact — no action warranted on existing holdings. NVDA's screener data confirms continued uptrend basing with massive EPS revision (+22.2%); hold.

CRITICAL CONTEXT: The track record is very poor — 11.1% win rate, profit factor 0.04x, Sortino -10.55. Five consecutive stops. This demands humility and conservatism. The instructions are explicit: do not force trades to manufacture alpha, and cash is a valid position. Accordingly, I am proposing just ONE new trade where the setup is genuinely asymmetric, not filling headroom for its own sake.

MARKET: SPY is in a mild uptrend (+1.41% 20d slope). Not a risk-off environment, but not screaming 'add risk' either. With 72% deployed and a struggling track record, adding a 5th position at modest size (bringing deployment to ~91%) is justifiable only for a high-conviction name.

BEST SETUP — TMUS: T-Mobile sits at just 22% of its 52-week range (basing in the lower half), trades at a fwd P/E of 12.63 and PEG of 0.64, generates $11.3B in free cash flow, and has been systematically taking subscriber share from AT&T and Verizon. At +0.7% above SMA50 with positive slope, it is early in the uptrend — not extended. R/R is over 3x with a clean 2x-ATR stop. Earnings are 38 days out (Oct 22), which is a known risk that will trigger a pre-earnings sizing review. All other extended names (APH 86% range, ANET 88%, ZBRA 82%, SCHW 78%, BMY 83%) are disqualified by the entry-timing rule. CTSH is cheap but +11.5% above SMA50 — too extended. EXE and EQT have revenue declines. No second trade is proposed — the evidence-based discipline of this account demands patience over activity.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $182 or better; if price pulls back to the SMA50 (~$181), that is the preferred entry. Do not chase above $185.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: T-Mobile is a quality compounder — $11.3B FCF, 25.2% op margin, fwd P/E 12.63, PEG 0.64. The company has structurally taken postpaid subscriber share from AT&T and Verizon for five consecutive years; that secular trend is intact. At 22% of the 52-week range, the market is pricing the business as if growth has stalled, but EPS revisions are +2.8% (positive, not deteriorating). Revenue +7.9% at this valuation is genuinely cheap for telecom quality. TECHNICAL: Price is just +0.7% above SMA50 with a positive slope; this is an early-stage uptrend, not an extended late-cycle entry. 52-week range position of 22% puts it firmly in basing territory. The 'extending' trend label reflects momentum direction, not price exhaustion — still -5% below SMA200, meaning meaningful recovery room. ATR 2.4% produces a clean 2x-ATR stop at $173.50, giving 4.8% downside with a 3.2x reward-to-risk.
trades.exit_plan: 1) Hard stop at $173.50 (2x ATR, no exceptions). 2) Pre-earnings review Oct 17 (5 days before Oct 22 earnings) — reduce or exit if position is underwater or if market regime deteriorates into downtrend. 3) Thesis break: material subscriber loss acceleration, margin compression below 20% op margin, or revenue guidance cut. 4) Time stop: if price is flat or lower after 90 days with no progress toward $195, reassess. 5) Take partial profits (~50%) near $200 to lock in gains if reached quickly.
